name: Map caption: storm
when: A weather beat on the map (storms, hurricanes). A storm drifts onto the coast, turning, its shadow darkening only the ground under it; the word lands on the calm left side. Nothing in it says flooding or damage.
anchor: The headline starts at 0.47 s and is in at 0.87 s: start the scene about half a second before the voice says the word.

vars.theme: clean or vice: the video's theme
vars.head: the word, in capitals as validated ("HURRICANES"); 13 characters at most so it stays clear of the storm
vars.source: who says it, as a sentence ("Confirmed by Rockstar"); empty = no source line
vars.map: the map image. Every position below is in pixels of this file at its natural size (map pixels). Empty = the map the skill ships: gta-map/maps/leonida.jpg, the whole state (its bounds are in gta-map/maps/maps.json).
vars.storm: the storm cloud: a square PNG with transparency, drawn 1500x1500 map pixels around its eye. Empty = the one the template ships (files/storm.png, our own procedural picture, not game art).
vars.storm_shadow: the storm's shadow: a square PNG, same size, drawn 34 px right and 46 px down of the cloud. Empty = the one the template ships (files/storm_shadow.png).
vars.storm_x: map x (map pixels) of the storm's eye when the scene starts. Default: offshore, east of the coast
vars.storm_y: map y of the storm's eye when the scene starts
vars.storm_x2: map x of the storm's eye when the scene ends: it drifts there over the whole scene (power1 out), turning -58 degrees every 6 s and growing from 90 to 100 %
vars.storm_y2: map y of the storm's eye when the scene ends
vars.cam_x: map x at the frame centre when the scene starts
vars.cam_y: map y at the frame centre when the scene starts
vars.zoom: scale when the scene starts: 1 = one map pixel per screen pixel
vars.cam_x2: map x at the frame centre when the scene ends: the camera pushes from start to end over the whole scene (sine in-out)
vars.cam_y2: map y at the frame centre when the scene ends
vars.out: seconds after the start: when the caption leaves (at least 1.5). The scene ends 0.3 s later, on the map

changed: The storm fades in over 15 frames instead of 20 (entry 0.5 s at most). Its turn keeps the validated rate (-58 degrees per 6 s) when the scene is longer or shorter. The map, the storm pictures, the storm's track and the camera are variables in map pixels instead of being built in.
